summary: @servicetitan/unit-tests preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs (itself minifier-obfuscated with _0x-style identifiers) probes for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads a Bun release zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, extracts the `bun` executable to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line file using string-array/VM obfuscation (rotated constant table with a `.push(.shift())` rotator function and opaque `_0x`-style identifiers) — content that is not inspectable by Node-based install-time review and whose purpose is unrelated to a unit-testing library. The public main entry is a trivial re-export of ts-mockito; the description is empty and the `@servicetitan` scope with repository `github.com/servicetitan/playground.git` provides brand-familiarity cover for an unrelated install-time payload. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute a bundled opaque blob during `npm install` is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and hands arbitrary code execution to whoever controls the payload on any machine running `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
